patient_group_explanation: Latex, fibres, silk, wool and henna that people touch or handle.

allergens.definition: Jute is a natural plant fibre used to make sacks, ropes, mats, carpets and bags. Dust is released when jute is processed, packed or handled.
allergens.interpretation_insight: This result shows IgE to jute. It matters mainly if you work with jute or sacks and your symptoms improve away from them. A positive result alone does not prove allergy or occupational disease. Your doctor can advise.
allergens.card_summary: A plant fibre used for sacks, ropes, mats and carpets at work.
allergens.caution: Dust from fibres can irritate the nose and chest without allergy. A blood test cannot decide this, so your work history matters.

allergens.definition: Treated sheep wool is wool that has been cleaned or processed for making yarn, blankets, carpets and clothing. It may still carry traces of animal proteins.
allergens.interpretation_insight: This result shows IgE to treated wool. Wool often irritates skin without being an allergy. A positive result alone does not prove allergy to wool. It matters more if you handle wool at work. Tell your doctor about any rash.
allergens.card_summary: Cleaned wool used for blankets, shawls, carpets and winter clothing at work.
allergens.caution: Itching from wool is usually irritation and not allergy. This test does not prove either, so discuss skin symptoms with a doctor.

allergens.definition: Silk is a fine fibre made by silkworms. It is used for sarees, scarves, bedding and fabrics, and is handled in silk reeling and weaving units.
allergens.interpretation_insight: This result shows IgE to silk. It matters mainly if you work with silk or silkworms and your symptoms improve away from work. A positive result alone does not prove allergy. Your doctor can advise you.
allergens.card_summary: A fine fibre from silkworms used in sarees, scarves, bedding and fabrics.
allergens.caution: Silkworm and silk exposure at work differs from wearing silk. A positive result needs your work history and a doctor's review.

allergens.definition: Latex is a natural rubber from the rubber tree. It is found in gloves, balloons, condoms, rubber bands, catheters and many medical and household products.
allergens.interpretation_insight: This result shows IgE to latex. A positive result alone does not prove latex allergy. Latex can cause serious reactions in some people, so tell your doctor and dentist about any past reactions to gloves or balloons.
allergens.card_summary: Natural rubber found in gloves, balloons, condoms and many medical and household products.
allergens.caution: If gloves or balloons have caused swelling, wheezing or collapse, seek medical advice before any procedure that uses latex products.

cross_reactivity.patient_note: Some people with latex reactions also react to certain fruits. Tell your doctor if these fruits have ever caused symptoms.

allergens.definition: Henna is a plant dye used as mehndi paste on skin and hair. It is applied for weddings, festivals, hair colouring and conditioning treatments at salons.
allergens.interpretation_insight: This result shows IgE to henna. Skin reactions to henna products are often caused by additives and not by henna itself. A blood test cannot decide this. Ask a dermatologist about any skin symptoms after using henna.
allergens.card_summary: A plant dye used as mehndi paste on skin, nails and hair.
allergens.caution: Rashes from mehndi and hair dyes are often skin contact reactions, which a blood IgE test does not measure.

allergens.definition: Cotton linters are the short fibres left on cotton seeds after the main cotton is removed. They are used in stuffing, paper and cellulose products.
allergens.interpretation_insight: This result shows IgE to cotton linters. It matters mainly if you work in cotton processing and your symptoms improve away from work. A positive result alone does not prove allergy or occupational disease. Your doctor can advise.
allergens.card_summary: Short cotton fibres used in stuffing, paper and cellulose products at work.
allergens.caution: Cotton dust can irritate the nose and chest without allergy. Wearing cotton clothes is not the same as this exposure.
